content.title: About
content.content: Canned ham is cooked or smoked pork meat packed in a sealed can and heat‑treated for long‑term storage. It is ready to eat straight from the can and is commonly used in salads, sandwiches, and hot dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned ham is popular in regions with limited access to fresh meat.
Cans are typically sterilized at 121 °C for 30‑45 minutes.
The product may contain additives such as salt, nitrites, flavorings, and sometimes sugar.
There is a “ham in its own juice” version that uses minimal added liquid.
Canned ham is often included in military rations because of its long shelf life.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ham provides about 15‑18 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Good source of B1, B3 and B12 vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Convenient and long‑lasting
items.content: Sealed cans allow storage for 3‑5 years without refrigeration.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Canned ham often contains 2‑3 g of salt per 100 g, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Nitrites and preservatives
items.content: Nitrites used to preserve color can form potentially harmful compounds when overheated.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pork proteins.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Ham contains saturated fats, so intake should be limited in cardiovascular disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ham can be eaten straight from the can, sliced into salads, added to pasta, omelets or hot sandwiches. If desired, briefly warm it in a pan, but avoid high heat to prevent nitrosamine formation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, refrigerate and consume within 5‑7 days.
